about.title: Napa Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Most people in Napa trust their care. When something goes wrong at a clinic in the Soscol Avenue corridor or during a hospital stay in Napa County, the first feeling is confusion rather than anger. Was this a known risk, or did someone miss something they should have caught? California law draws that line. A poor result by itself is not malpractice; there has to be a departure from the standard of care that caused harm, and a qualified medical expert almost always has to say so. Timing matters too. Under MICRA, you generally have one year from when you discovered the injury, and never more than three years from when it happened, plus a 90-day notice must go to the provider before a lawsuit is filed. We handle medical negligence claims on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. You describe what happened; our team tells you whether it is worth pursuing.

whyChoose.title: Why Napa Residents Choose Us for Malpractice Questions

items.title: MICRA's clock is short and specific
items.desc: One year from discovery, three years at the outside, and a 90-day notice before filing. We can pin down which dates apply to your situation before any of them slip past.

items.title: An expert has to weigh in
items.desc: California requires a qualified medical professional to support nearly every malpractice claim. Our team knows how to get records reviewed by the right specialty early, so you are not left guessing.

items.title: Honest screening, no pressure
items.desc: A bad outcome is not automatically negligence, and we will tell you that plainly. Because we work on contingency, you pay nothing unless there is a recovery.

items.question: I was treated in a Napa emergency room after a crash on Rt 29 and a fracture was missed. Is that malpractice?
items.answer: Possibly, but it depends on what a reasonably careful emergency physician would have done with the same symptoms and imaging. Napa saw 357 people injured in collisions in 2025, and ER visits after crashes are common, so these cases come up. We would have your films and chart reviewed by a qualified expert to see whether the standard of care was met.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover in a California malpractice case?
items.answer: MICRA caps non-economic damages, such as pain and emotional distress, and that cap rises each year under current law. Economic losses like medical bills and lost income are handled separately. Our team can explain how the cap applies to the year your claim is filed.

items.question: What does it cost to have us review my case?
items.answer: Nothing. We handle medical negligence claims on contingency, so there is no fee unless your case results in a recovery.
